## 3. The evidence that moved it


**The agentic thread opens, and the corpus can date it to the day.**
[ESCARGOT](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39842860/) is published on 4 February
2025: an LLM agent reasoning over biomedical knowledge graphs. The first title
using the word *agentic* follows
[four days later](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39922663/). Everything this
corpus later says about agentic diffusion — into oncology journals in June, to
wet-lab-adjacent work in August, into the immunology journals in December — is
measured from here.

**Two randomized trials of AI interventions, in the same journal, in the same
month**: [GPT-4 assistance for physician performance](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39910272/)
and [AI-individualized treatment of persistent atrial fibrillation](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39953289/).
Neither title states a direction. This matters for a claim the corpus made and
later withdrew: randomized AI trials were never rare in 2025, and none of them
reported a null in its title.

**A protein language model claims to simulate 500 million years of evolution**
([39818825](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39818825/), *Science*), and a
[cell atlas foundation model](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39566551/) makes
scalable search over human cells the deliverable. Both are capability claims with
no evaluation adversary in the month — the audit genre is running at roughly one
paper in seventy here, against one in ten by December.

## 4. Refutations

### (a) Landing on a tracked thread

Three Treg inversions in one month, all outside oncology and all saying the same
thing: [meningeal Tregs preserve brain homeostasis](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39873623/),
[recirculating Tregs mediate thymic regeneration](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39892391/),
and [terminal effector Treg persistence is essential to prevent intestinal
inflammation](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39905200/). The last is the
sharpest for anyone designing a depletion strategy: the effector-Treg
compartment that tumour immunology wants removed is the compartment gut
immunology finds indispensable.

[39789375](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39789375/) (*Nat Immunol*):
**low-avidity** T cells drive endogenous tumour immunity in mice and humans. The
selection logic under neoantigen prioritisation ranks candidates by predicted
binding strength; this says the cells that matter are the ones that logic
discards.

[39972134](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39972134/): clonal driver neoantigens
are lost under EGFR TKI and immune selection pressure — the first of what becomes
a recurring attack on the size of the target space.

### (b) Method credibility

[39870925](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39870925/) (*Nature*): retraction of
a published mechanism for the suppression of homologous recombination in G1
cells.

[39820264](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39820264/) (*JAMA*): limited evidence
supports more than forty predictive machine learning algorithms *already in use*
in primary care. The gap between deployment and evidence is stated as a count.

[39660643](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39660643/): chromatin deep learning
models' expression predictions depend on histone mark function, regulatory
distance and cellular state rather than on anything general — an early instance
of the pattern that dominates 2026, where the model's apparent capability turns
out to be a property of the evaluation.

[39809900](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39809900/): a failed reproduction, in
*Nature Genetics*, of a published disease-resistance gene in wheat.
